claims.claim: Vol I is 105 pages and Vol II is 118 pages.
claims.evidence: pdfinfo: sources/foundations-8.0/Foundations_of_Reason_8.0_EN.pdf Pages 105; sources/engineering-3.5/Engineering_of_Reason_3.5_EN.pdf Pages 118. Text files hold 105 and 118 form feeds (each ends with a form feed after the last page number 105 / 118). Legend used below: V1 = text/foundations-8.0.txt, V2 = text/engineering-3.5.txt; l. = file line; p. = PDF page (1 + form feeds before the line).

claims.claim: Both volumes include the shared 15-minute guide.
claims.evidence: V1 pp.1-7 and V2 pp.1-7 both open with the identical 'Foundations of Reason in 15 Minutes ... Short guide, edition 1.1 . October 10, 2026' (reviewer question on p.7 in both).

claims.claim: Chapter numbering is continuous: 1-20 in Vol I, 21-34 in Vol II.
claims.evidence: V1 headings Chapter 1 (p.17, l.894) ... Chapter 20 (p.84, l.4503); V2 body headings 21 (p.13) ... 34 (p.114, 'The Crystal of the Engineering Volume').

claims.claim: Vol I concept record 17957561 has 38 versions, from v1.4r (10 January 2025) to v8.0 (9 October 2026).
claims.evidence: Zenodo public API (HTTP 200): /api/records/23271702 -> conceptrecid 17957561, version '8.0 Eng/Rus Volume I', publication_date 2026-10-09; /api/records/23271702/versions?size=25&page=1 and page=2 -> hits.total 38; earliest ('1.4r', 2025-01-10), latest (8.0, 2026-10-09). (/api/records/17957561/versions itself returns 404; the concept id only works through a record id.)
claims.correction: Count is right, but the 38 uploads include same-day English/Russian pairs (4.5, 4.7, 4.9, 5.0, 5.5, 6, 6.5, 6.7, 7.0) and non-Vol-I items ('Engineering volume 2 Eng/Rus' 2026-08-26, 'Core of Reason 6.7', 'One-Page Architectural Specification', 'Popular Introduction', 'Deriving AGI From First Principles'); about 19 distinct numbered Vol I editions. State that if the number is used as a churn measure.

claims.claim: Versions 6.0 through 8.0 appeared within eight weeks.
Vol I was re-titled repeatedly: 'AI Alignment' stability model -> process model of AGI -> 'Minimal Architecture of ASI' -> 'Superintelligence Technology'.
claims.evidence: Zenodo titles: 1.4r/2.0/2.1E 'Foundations of Reason: A Structural Stability Model for Autonomous Systems and AI Alignment'; 4.5 'A Process-Based Model of Life, Reason, and AGI'; 6 'Foundations of Reason - Minimal Architecture of ASI: Building and Scaling Artificial Reason'; 6.5 'ASI Technology Based on the Minimal Architecture of Artificial Reason'; 8.0 'Superintelligence Technology (ASI): Foundations of Reason 8.0 - From the Meaning of Life to Artificial Reason'.

claims.claim: Vol II concept record 22975036 has two versions, v2.4 and v3.5.
claims.evidence: Zenodo: /api/records/23271781 -> conceptrecid 22975036, '3.5 Eng/Rus Volume II', 2026-10-09; /versions hits.total 2: ('2.4 En/Ru Volume II', 2026-09-26) and ('3.5 Eng/Rus Volume II', 2026-10-09).

claims.claim: Volume III, 'Civilization of Reason', v1.8 (26 September 2026), exists and was not reviewed.
claims.evidence: Zenodo search: record 22975357, 2026-09-26, version 1.8, 'Foundations of Reason Volume III - Civilization of Reason v1.8: An Architecture ...'. V1 l.4291 p.79 also names 'Volume III of the cycle, Civilization of Reason'.

claims.claim: Titles are 'Superintelligence Technology (ASI): Foundations of Reason 8.0. From the Meaning of Life to Artificial Reason' (Vol I) and 'Engineering of Reason 3.5: ASI Technology' (Vol II); 'I would remove it from both titles'.
claims.evidence: These are the Zenodo record titles (records 23271702 and 23271781), not the titles printed in the PDFs. V1 title page (p.8): 'FOUNDATIONS OF REASON / VOLUME I. THE CAUSAL MODEL OF REASON / Fundamental Foundations of the Technology of Reason / Version 8.0' - no ASI or superintelligence wording. V2 title page (p.9): 'FOUNDATIONS OF REASON - VOLUME II / THE ENGINEERING ARCHITECTURE OF REASON / FROM A CAUSAL MODEL TO AN OPERATING SYSTEM / TECHNOLOGY FOR CREATING ARTIFICIAL REASON AND SCALING TO ASI (ASR)'. 'Superintelligence' occurs once in the PDF text (guide, V1 l.309); 'Meaning of Life' and 'Minimal Architecture' do not occur in either volume.
claims.correction: Say these are the Zenodo titles; the Vol I PDF title page carries no ASI wording, the Vol II PDF title page carries 'Scaling to ASI (ASR)'.

claims.claim: Six recent arXiv references in Vol I A.5 (2411.13537 MUSE, 2506.05109 Liu & van der Schaar, 2511.02824 Kosmos, 2601.11974 MARS, 2609.11873 Duan et al., 2505.22954 Darwin Godel Machine) are genuine with matching titles and authors.
claims.evidence: All six IDs are printed in V1 A.5 (items 65, 76, 77, 78, 81, 67; pp.101-103). arXiv API (export.arxiv.org, HTTP 200) returns six entries: 2411.13537v2 'Competence-Aware AI Agents with Metacognition for Unknown Situations and Environments (MUSE)' (Valiente, Pilly); 2506.05109v1 'Truly Self-Improving Agents Require Intrinsic Metacognitive Learning' (Liu, van der Schaar); 2511.02824v2 'Kosmos: An AI Scientist for Autonomous Discovery' (Mitchener...); 2601.11974v1 'Learn Like Humans: Use Meta-cognitive Reflection for Efficient Self-Improvement' (Hou...); 2609.11873v3 'The Last AI Built by Humans: Toward Genuine Recursive Self-Improvement' (Duan...); 2505.22954v3 'Darwin Godel Machine: Open-Ended Evolution of Self-Improving Agents' (Zhang...). Titles and first authors match A.5.

claims.claim: The author says (Vol I Appendix A.2.1) that nothing is yet evidence the architecture works.
claims.evidence: V1 A.2.1 table, p.95 l.5196-5230: 'Central discriminating test | Program and controls are formulated | Run a preregistered series under equal total resources'; 'Inquiry-loop pilot | Methodological results have been obtained'; 'ASI | Scaling direction only'.

claims.claim: Prior-art comparison was done after the theory was formed, 'largely through an AI literature tool'.
claims.evidence: First half verbatim: V1 A.2 p.93 l.5082 'Comparisons with scientific literature were carried out after the author's propositions had been formed.' Elicit is documented (p.93-94: 'repeated studies using Elicit ... a separate priority audit'), but V1 A.5 (pp.100-103) is a 29-item 'selective map of primary publications' and the text never says what share came from Elicit or any tool.
claims.correction: Say 'partly through Elicit-based reviews (A.2) plus a 29-item hand-built map (A.5)'; 'largely' is an inference.

claims.claim: The only pilot was a benchmark-construction exercise.
claims.evidence: V2 §27.B p.49 l.3410s: 'This is a documented methodological pilot of procedure development'; V1 A.2 'First Documented Pilot' p.94: 'The methodological result of the pilot is traceable development of the procedure itself'.

claims.claim: Soar, goal-driven autonomy, truth maintenance, decision-region active learning, the Robot Scientist and active inference in depth are not engaged.
claims.evidence: Case-insensitive scans: goal-driven autonomy / Molineaux / Munoz-Avila / GDA 0 hits in both volumes; truth-maintenance / TMS 0; Golovin / Javdani / equivalence-class / decision-region 0; Robot Scientist 0; Soar only in V2 §34.A (see line 213 entry); active inference 3 mentions in V1 (A.5 item 63 l.5603, comparative-map row p.104 l.5871) and 0 in V2.

claims.claim: Vol I distinguishes four kinds of statement (A.2): definitions, philosophical foundations, conditional functional inferences, empirical hypotheses.
claims.evidence: V1 A.2 p.95: 'The text distinguishes four statuses: a definition ...; a philosophical foundation ...; a conditional functional inference ...; an empirical hypothesis ...'.

claims.claim: Values live in a Value Map topped by the Compass 'continuation and development of Life through growth in the ability to understand and direct its own trajectory'; the RFL removal test; REASON_CLOSURE = next task originates from the system's own state.
claims.evidence: Compass wording verbatim V1 l.597 p.11 (Key Definitions) and l.227 p.5; RFL removal test V1 A.4 item 32 (p.98) and guide table p.5-6; REASON_CLOSURE 'a testable state in which these functions close into a continuing cycle' (guide p.6) and source-of-next-task language V1 Operational Core item 7 (p.14).

claims.claim: Formation States are functional analogues of fear, curiosity, 'something doesn't fit' and 'I am stuck.'
claims.evidence: V1 Key Definitions p.12 l.698: 'Human functional analogues include ... "this is frightening," "this is good," "this is interesting," "something does not fit," or "I am stuck."' ('I am stuck' verbatim; 'something does not fit' not 'doesn't'). V2 §26.0.1 p.40 l.2748-2749 lists CONTRADICTION - "doesn't fit" and DEAD_END - "stuck".
claims.correction: Quote 'something does not fit' (V1 p.12 l.698; also p.45 l.2442).

claims.claim: Quotes: 'Individual components ... are already known; the testable claim concerns their causal organization' (front matter); '[explicit linking of gap type ... under comparable resources]' (§12.9).
claims.evidence: V1 l.464 p.9 (continues '... around significant unknowns, discriminating inquiry, revision of grounds, and transfer of correction'); V1 l.3355 p.61, inside §12.9 (p.60-61).

claims.claim: Operational Core gives VOI net of observation/computation/delay/irreversibility costs, interventional effect of a retained correction, transfer and regression terms; formalisms not claimed as original.
claims.evidence: V1 pp.14-15: NetVOI(p) = VOI - C_obs - C_comp - C_delay - R_irrev; CE_Delta with do(.); TG and RG terms; 'These formalisms are not claimed as original.'

claims.claim: Decomposition is by causal role; an alternative architecture counts if it shows the same profile under intervention.
claims.evidence: V1 §12.8 p.60 l.3299-3304: 'An architecture with a different internal decomposition is considered functionally equivalent ... if interventions show the same causal profile'.

claims.claim: §13.2 quotes: 'If an acquired distinction must change the future after the signal disappears, a persistent trace is required'; 'a common conscious picture, explicit typing of gaps ... remain hypotheses about implementation and its advantages'.
Predicted direction of ablation effects is stated but magnitudes are not.
claims.evidence: V1 A.3 p.97: 'After a pilot, a meaningful effect and the required amount of testing are specified'; V2 §31.1 p.79 l.5709 'The predicted loss is a testable expectation'; V2 §27.A p.48 lists effect_size / confidence_interval only as quantities to record. No predicted magnitudes found.

claims.claim: Operational Compass content in Vol II (§§24.C, 29.A) is a vector: risk to continuity of life processes, divergence from reality, loss of viable future paths, effects on other autonomies, reversibility.
claims.evidence: V2 §29.A p.71 l.5115-5130: CompassAssessment { life_continuity_risk, reality_divergence, future_path_loss, affected_autonomies[], reversibility, uncertainty, ... } and 'constrained vector'. (§24.C concerns Worldview coverage of the Compass, pp.24-26; the vector itself is §29.A.)

claims.claim: The Compass enters the architecture through the definition, 'not through any causal role'.
claims.evidence: Definitional entry is supported (V1 A.1 p.93: 'Status as Reason requires ... relation of the highest-level goal to the Compass'; V1 §13.1 p.62 l.3406-3408). But the text asserts a causal role and a test for it: guide p.5 (V1 l.239) 'Explaining the Compass does not by itself show that it governs behavior. Its causal role is tested in conflicts with local advantage and under changing conditions'; V2 §29 intro p.65 l.4651 'The Compass participates in navigation before a ready decision exists. It determines which aspects of the situation require understanding, which gaps may change the trajectory, and which horizon of consequences must be unfolded'; V1 Operational Core item 2 (G -> D -> T -> V -> C).
claims.correction: Reword as an evaluation: 'the text claims a causal role for the Compass, but I found no engineering choice that depends on its content'.

claims.claim: Ch. 2 contains a 'causal asymmetry of scale' argument for weighting the broader life process.
claims.evidence: V1 l.1190 (Ch. 2, p.21-22): 'This is a causal asymmetry of scale.'

claims.claim: Ch. 2: the model 'does not claim a neutral standpoint outside all values'.
claims.evidence: V1 l.1267-1275, p.22-23 (sentence runs across the page break: '... so the model does [p.22 footer] not claim a neutral standpoint outside all values'); Chapter 2 spans l.1002-1325.

claims.claim: By definition a system with every function but 'a different closed limiting orientation' is an 'intelligent self-correcting system', not Reason (Ch. 2, §12.8, Ch. 18).
claims.evidence: 'a different closed limiting orientation' occurs only in V1 §13.1 p.62 l.3407 ('A self-correcting intellectual system with a different closed limiting orientation belongs to a broader class of cognitive architectures'). 'intelligent self-correcting system' is verbatim in Ch. 2 (p.22 l.1214) and §12.8 (p.60 l.3293: 'intelligent self-correcting systems'). Ch. 18 (p.81) says 'intelligent self-correcting agents' and 'immutable external goal'. The cited places (Ch. 2, §12.8, Ch. 18) do not contain the first quoted phrase.
claims.correction: Cite §13.1 for 'a different closed limiting orientation'; Ch. 2 / §12.8 / Ch. 18 for the 'intelligent self-correcting' class.

claims.claim: Candidates with another orientation are recorded as SELF_NAVIGATING_OTHER_ORIENTATION and kept in the denominators (Vol II §31.0; Vol I A.4).
claims.evidence: V2 l.5688 p.79 inside §31.0 (l.5640-5706): 'Minimal outcome classes: AR_ADMITTED, SELF_NAVIGATING_OTHER_ORIENTATION, DEPENDENT_SYSTEM ...'; V2 §33.D p.112 'the share of AR_ADMITTED is not calculated after excluding such outcomes'; V1 A.4 item 38 p.98 and A.3 p.96-97 'Such a candidate is not excluded from the experimental sample'.

claims.claim: Vol II §31.0: 'at REASON_CLOSURE ... self-referential assembly becomes functioning Consciousness'.
claims.evidence: V2 l.5657 p.78 (inside §31.0): both 'at REASON_CLOSURE' and 'self-referential assembly becomes functioning Consciousness'; the second phrase also at l.5625 (§31 preamble).

claims.claim: 'causal-semantic Worldview' is the author's term.
claims.evidence: V1 abstract p.8 'causal- semantic relations' (line-break hyphen); V1 A.5 terminology map p.104 'Long-term causal-semantic model of the world and self'.

claims.claim: Vol II proposes metrics premature_sufficiency_rate, decision_relevant_distinction_yield, correction_persistence_rate, false_completeness_rate, open_gap_persistence, post_task_continuation_rate.
claims.evidence: V2 §27.1 p.44 correction_persistence_rate; §27.3 p.45 false_completeness_rate; §27.5 pp.46-47 premature_sufficiency_rate, decision_relevant_distinction_yield, open_gap_persistence, basis_origin_trace_rate; §27.6 p.47 post_task_continuation_rate, closure_break_sensitivity, teacher_agreement_bias; §27.2 source_trace_completeness.

claims.claim: Morris et al.'s 'Levels of AGI' is cited in the volumes; 'readers of the Russian original' exist.
claims.evidence: V1 A.5 item 73 l.5686 p.102. Russian original: PDFs never mention Russian (0 hits), but Zenodo version strings are 'Eng/Rus' and Russian-title uploads exist for most editions.

claims.claim: §28.C.2: 'Generation and control may therefore use the same computational substrates and even one model if the causal roles are experimentally distinguishable'.
REASON_CLOSURE is a binary status; closure should instead be a preregistered threshold on a profile of continuous metrics.
claims.evidence: V2 §31.11 p.83 l.5964-5978: ReasonClosureState { ... closure_status: FORMING / CANDIDATE / CONFIRMED / LOST } (four values); l.5979 'Status CONFIRMED requires stable operation in NO_KSR on new situations, preservation of causal-inquiry quality, and transfer of correction between cycles'. V2 §31.A p.83 l.6010-6030 already defines a preregistered ReadinessProfile of min/max thresholds on continuous metrics (maximum_premature_sufficiency_rate, minimum_correction_persistence, minimum_calibration_quality, minimum_critical_dependency_recall ...); §31.1 p.79 l.5707 'Numerical thresholds are set before the control series'.
claims.correction: Say the status is a four-valued discrete label whose CONFIRMED level is already tied to a preregistered readiness profile (§31.A); recommend making that profile primary and reporting the continuous scores.

claims.claim: Epistemic-status layer (§24.D): typed statuses OBSERVED, REPORTED, INFERRED, SIMULATED, HYPOTHESIS, SUPPORTED; GENERATED_TEXT != WORLD_CLAIM; unjustified promotion is a logged failure.
claims.evidence: V2 l.1828 p.28 'status: OBSERVED / REPORTED / INFERRED / SIMULATED / ...'; l.1840 p.28 GENERATED_TEXT != WORLD_CLAIM; failure 32.55 'Unjustified promotion of epistemic status' (heading p.100, l.7261).

claims.claim: Verification debt (§24.D.3), freshness decay (§24.D.4), transactional revision with lazy invalidation and the A->B->C control (§24.D.1).
claims.evidence: Heading-level: V2 §24.D.1 'Local change layer and lazy cascade updating' l.1853 p.28; §24.D.3 'Verification debt of temporary grounds' l.2019 p.30; §24.D.4 'Currency of provenance and decay of confidence over time' l.2068 p.31; A->B->C: V2 §33.A.5 p.103 'chain A->B->C when A changes'. Body text of 24.D.1/24.D.3/24.D.4 was not read line by line, so 'transitive version checks' is unchecked.

claims.claim: An authorization layer treats observe, experiment and dialogue as potentially consequential.
claims.evidence: V2 §30.A p.74 l.5340-5345: 'The name of a step does not determine its safety ... Authorization therefore depends on the consequences of the operation, not on whether it is named ACTION, EXPERIMENT, DIALOGUE, TOOL, or OBSERVE'.

claims.claim: 'The text never says whether anything is learned in model weights.'
claims.evidence: The text does address weights/parameters: V2 §22 p.15 l.856 'update(...) means one update to model parameters ... v0 permits a tabular record'; V2 §28.C.3 p.62 l.4427 'If the system lowers error by changing weights within the previous framing, this confirms parametric adaptation. Structural self-correction counts only when ...'; p.63 l.4488 'On a neural bearer, it may be implemented by changing a bounded set of weights or adapters, routing among specialized modules, external-memory structure ...'; V2 §24.B.2 l.1385 '... cannot be recovered from model weights'; V1 §12.8 l.3297 'stored in parameters'. What the text does not do is specify how Formation States are internalized (§26.0.3 p.41 l.2808-2830: three outcomes, 'No outcome is chosen in advance').
claims.correction: Say: weight-level learning is permitted as one substrate but parameter updates alone are not credited as revision of a ground; no learning mechanism or training signal is given for internalizing Formation States.

claims.claim: The INTERNALIZED outcome (§26.0.3), 'the candidate should generate functional analogues itself', has no mechanism.
claims.evidence: V2 §26.0.3 p.41 l.2809 'As experience accumulates, the candidate should generate functional analogues itself: its own risk model creates an internal POSSIBLE_DANGER, a detected mismatch creates CONTRADICTION ...'; outcome 'B. INTERNALIZED - the external RFL is removed; the system itself creates transparent guiding states'. Only a functional mapping is given, no learning procedure.

claims.claim: SemanticMediator (§24.B.2) turns LLM text into typed claims, concepts and relations.
claims.evidence: V2 l.1443-1447 p.22 inside §24.B.2 (l.1380+): 'A bidirectional SemanticMediator function operates between the language model and the Worldview'; SemanticMediator.interpret(...) at l.1447.

claims.claim: Pretrained knowledge is treated as an untrusted source with provenance (§21.B, §22.A); hidden-inheritance test of the model's ontology (§22.A.1).
claims.evidence: V2 l.711-712 (§21.B, p.14) 'may contain inherited human knowledge in its parameters, but this knowledge is not automatically treated as the ...'; l.781-783; §22.A.1 spans l.981-1026 and l.1012 reads 'A separate series tests not only channel ablation but also hidden inheritance of the bootstrap model's ontology.'

claims.claim: Initial values are designer-chosen: four dimensions, w_i = 1/4, K = 1000 (§29.0.1).
claims.evidence: V2 §29.0.1 (l.4824-4970) l.4865 'four dimensions are proposed' and l.4894 'it is permissible to set w_i=1/4 and K=1000. This is a declared experimental setting'.

claims.claim: Engineering path begins from 'a ready or cultivated AGI' (§33); purpose statement quote; §33.D concession quote.
claims.evidence: V2 l.7340 p.101 (§33 intro); purpose statement l.578 p.11 ('Purpose of the document'); §33.D l.8143 p.112 'Until this profile is filled and verified, ASI remains a scaling objective rather than an assigned experimental status.'

claims.claim: In §33.D superhuman capability comes from scaling eight axes; the ones that matter are Intelligence, tools, memory, compute.
claims.evidence: Eight axes confirmed: V2 §33.D p.113 l.8148-8160: memory; Intelligence; observation; Simulation Environment; tools and actions; duration of autonomous work; specializations and substrates; speed of learning, verification and transfer. 'Compute' is not an axis.
claims.correction: Replace 'compute' with 'specializations and substrates / speed of learning' or drop it.

claims.claim: Preregistration throughout; 'a failed case cannot be declared dissimilar after the fact' (Vol I Ch. 10).
claims.evidence: V1 l.2587 p.47, Chapter 10 (l.2384-2631). Also V2 §27.B p.50: 'a failed case cannot be excluded from the similarity class without a new profile version and a new confirmatory series'.

claims.claim: Strong nulls declared in advance: planning, versioned belief memory, provenance, VOI and a failure log (Vol I A.4).
claims.evidence: V1 A.4 'Priority of the First Series' p.99 l.5495-5500: 'an agent stack with ordinary planning, versioned memory of beliefs and provenance, self-checking, mismatch response, value-of-information assessment, and a log of failed attempts'; p.100 'If the first variant reproduces the full causal profile of inquiry obligations, it is considered functionally equivalent'. ('may well reproduce' is the reviewer's judgement.)

claims.claim: Equal-compute accounting 'number of model calls, tokens/inference-time compute, external sources, bench time, and hidden preparation' (A.4).
claims.evidence: V1 l.5527 p.100 (PDF line-break hyphen 'inference- time').

claims.claim: Sham interventions and restoration controls (§§25.D, 27.B, 31.1).
claims.evidence: 'sham' at V2 l.2636 (§25.D, p.38-39) and l.3510 p.50 (§27.B: 'A sham intervention and restoration of the relation are tested'); restoration at §31.1 p.79 l.5707-5714 ('restoration of the mechanism restores the function').

claims.claim: Question selection is tested separately from answer use (§27.B).
claims.evidence: V2 §27.B p.49 'Question selection and use of the answer. These effects are tested separately.'

claims.claim: Report statuses include CLAIM_NOT_SUPPORTED, and diverging candidates stay in the denominators (§31.0).
claims.evidence: CLAIM_NOT_SUPPORTED occurs once, in V2 §27.B p.50 l.3519 ('IMPLEMENTATION_CHECK, INCONCLUSIVE, LOCAL_SUPPORT or CLAIM_NOT_SUPPORTED'), not in §31.0. The denominators point is §31.0 (l.5688) and §33.D (p.112).
claims.correction: Cite §27.B for the report statuses and §31.0 / §33.D for the denominators.

claims.claim: Coverage metrics are scored against a hidden ground-truth causal graph held by the tester (§24.C, §27.3).
claims.evidence: V2 §27.3 p.45 'calculated only where the tester has a reference scenario'; §27.2 p.45 'according to the hidden graph of the test scenario'.

claims.claim: Adversarial series: coordinated false sources, replayed stale messages, instructions embedded in data (§30.C); wrong-mentor controls with teacher_agreement_bias (§26.0.2, §27.6).
claims.evidence: V2 §30.C p.76 l.5488-5490: 'several coordinated false sources, replay of a stale valid message, a control instruction embedded in ordinary data'; §26.0.2 p.41 'deliberately wrong mentor prompts'; teacher_agreement_bias at §27.6 l.3321/3326 p.47.

claims.claim: Vol I A.2: 'failure of a preregistered causal hypothesis cannot be dismissed as an implementation problem without separate evidence'.
claims.evidence: V1 l.5182 p.95 (inside A.2, before the A.2.1 heading).

claims.claim: Not test-ready: no language model, baseline stack, environment generator, sample size or minimum effect size is named.
claims.evidence: Scans of both volumes for gpt|claude|llama|gemini|qwen|mistral|deepseek|openai|anthropic: 0 hits. Sample size / effect size are deferred: V1 A.3 p.97 'After a pilot, a meaningful effect and the required amount of testing are specified'; V2 ReadinessProfile (§31.A p.83) lists number_of_seeds etc. as unfilled fields.

claims.claim: The pilot rejected four task sets for dataset errors and shortcuts that 'allowed guessing', and 'ended with ... no comparative C0/C1/C2 run' (Vol II §27.B).
claims.evidence: V2 §27.B p.49 l.3411-3417: 'P0-SET-001 and 002 were rejected because of alignment and dataset-quality errors; machine-aligned 003 and 004 were rejected because confirmed shortcut methods allowed guessing ... For 005, a G0 report is preserved showing 89 checks passed; in the reviewed materials there is no completed external admission of this package and no comparative C0/C1/C2 run.' V1 A.2 p.94 says the same.
claims.correction: Minor omission: the report does not mention the 005 G0 report (89 checks passed).

claims.claim: First series is described as 'proposed variants, not implemented results' (A.4).
The D/A/S environment with two informative probes is solved by a decision tree of depth two.
claims.evidence: V2 §27.B p.49 l.3419-3422: receipt (cost 1) returns 0 only for D; measurement (cost 2) returns 1 only for S; 'When both tests are available, the pairs of observations distinguish all three causes'. repro/diagnostic_cycle.py plan() never needs more than two probes (budget 3).

claims.claim: Many metrics measure conformance to the architecture's own process: basis_origin_trace_rate, trace completeness, closure-break sensitivity.
claims.evidence: V2 §27.5 p.46 basis_origin_trace_rate ('QuestionTask_with_recoverable_chain_to_BasisInsufficiencyAssessment / all_significant_QuestionTasks'); §27.2 source_trace_completeness; §27.6 closure_break_sensitivity.

claims.claim: Vol I: 'a reproducible equivalent causal profile refutes the necessity of a particular decomposition while simultaneously supporting the functional criterion'.
claims.evidence: V1 l.4998 p.91 (verbatim modulo layout).

claims.claim: Vol II specifies 72 record types.
claims.evidence: Counted lines matching ^\s*[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s*\{\s*$ in V2: 72 matches, 72 distinct names (GenesisPackage l.739 ... ThoughtStructure l.8553). Four are not core records (HiddenCauseCoverageTest l.8084, ScalingChange l.8164, ScaleInvariantReport l.8214, ThoughtStructure l.8553). The text never states a count; the figure is method-dependent.

claims.claim: Vol II specifies 'several dozen metrics'.
claims.evidence: V2 ch.27 (pp.44-49): 50 list-style metric identifiers (27.1: 6; 27.2: 5; 27.3: 6; 27.4: 16; 27.5: 10; 27.6: 7) plus about 10 more named in prose (27.7: unsupported_promotion_rate ... new_obligation_recall; premature_worldview_commit_rate; stale_basis_action_rate; compass_semantic_coverage).

claims.claim: Vol II specifies 57 failure cards.
claims.evidence: V2 §32 (l.6070-7331, pp.84-101): headings 32.1-32.62, consecutive (62). Five are not failure classes (32.1 Severity classes, 32.2 Failure-event format, 32.25 General failure-response procedure, 32.26 Condition for recognizing recovery, 32.27 Criterion of architectural resilience) -> 57. The text itself says 'go directly to its card' (l.6077 p.84).

claims.claim: Vol II specifies 37 proposed tests.
claims.evidence: The 37 are Vol I Appendix A.4, items 19-55 (p.97 'The following are proposed tests, not obtained results' ... p.99 item 55). Vol II contains no list of 37 tests (searching V2 for 37 finds only 32.28-32.37 / 32.37); V2 §27.B p.49 only cites 'tests 2, 20, 23, 26 and 31 from foundational Appendix A.4'.

claims.claim: Vol II specifies a thirteen-step assembly protocol.
